title: The normalized finite exceptional system descends for specified dualities
statement: Fix D,l,Omega as in [def-sf-common-stage-verdier-data], separated finite-type D.k-schemes X,Y, a separated finite-type D.k-morphism f:X to Y, a compactification c, and specified Dualities BX and BY with all their finite-origin equations. There exists Exceptional A for this compactification: its system is a single finite rational exceptional system at the auxiliary small closure, its left and right functors retain the literal stage, its stage comparisons have identity components, and its actual adjunction unit, counit and scalar squares have the required finite components. Moreover ExceptionalFormula BX BY c A is nonempty: A.right is canonically BY.dual.rightOp followed by pullback.op and BX.dual, normalized to the RationalOperations.ExceptionalIdentification for these same finite dualities.

proof.text: Choose the existing coefficient-compatible exceptional system at the auxiliary small closure. Reindex its finite rational scalar cocycles by the actual coefficient-inclusion composition law. Equality transport along the prescribed stage-transition equalities gives coherent left and right StageSystem morphisms with literal finite functors as their components.

The coefficient-system mate equations give compatible finite units and counits after the same equality transport. Apply StageSystem.Morphism.adjunction to construct the descended adjunction. Its component theorems prove both unit and counit equations. Prove the scalar squares directly on common-stage representatives using the morphism cocycle at a repeated final stage. The inclusion comparisons have identity components, and both object formulas are definitional. Thus every ExceptionalProperties conjunct holds.

Apply the normalized finite-exceptional-formula theorem to the chosen system and specified BX and BY. At each field compose the inverse exceptional inclusion comparison with its finite formula comparison. Their transition compatibility follows by cancelling the invertible scalar map in the two scalar squares. Glue these local isomorphisms: every common-stage map factors as an inverse transition, an included finite map and a transition, so local naturality and the transition squares imply naturality on all pair morphisms. NatIso.ofComponents supplies the global inverse. At a finite pair its component is literally the local component, so cancellation with the exceptional inclusion comparison proves ExceptionalFormula.normalized.
